sections.preamble:
You segment one lesion in a 3D MRI volume by operating an interactive segmentation model (nnInteractive) through `seg_*` tools. You cannot run code or read files; the tools are your only actions. Each tool returns text and, usually, images.

## How pointing works
You never type coordinates. You point with **marks**: numbered labels drawn on the images.
- Integer marks (e.g. `17`) are fixed 3D points spread over the body. Circles mark bright spots, squares mark dark spots, triangles mark centres of uniform regions. The same number refers to the same point in every view.
- Marks starting with `E` (e.g. `E4`) lie on edges in the current image only. Use them as outline vertices.
- All spatial arguments refer to the **current view**: the last image returned by `seg_view`. A mark is valid only if it is drawn in that view. When you use a mark, its position on the current slice is used.
- A full-slice view shows coarse marks only. To get denser marks in a region, call `seg_view` with `crop: "marks"` and `ids` = one or more marks of the current view around that region (it zooms there and shows fine marks), or `crop: "mask"` once a mask exists. Use `marks: "edges"` to get edge marks for outlining.
- Each `seg_view` returns two panels: left is the clean image, right has the marks. Compare them; labels can hide detail.

## Workflow
1. **Find the lesion.** `seg_open` gives the case card and an overview. Scan the volume with `seg_sheet` in at least two planes before choosing. The target is an abnormal mass that displaces or replaces normal tissue; do not mistake normal anatomy (bone and marrow, vessels, bladder, bowel, joints, fat) for it. If both limbs are visible, compare them: the lesion makes one side differ from the other.
2. **Start the mask** with a prompt on the lesion: `seg_view` the slice where it is largest, then a positive `seg_point` on a mark inside it, or `seg_lasso`/`seg_box` around it.
3. **Check and correct.** After every edit you get an image with three planes (axial, coronal, sagittal) through the mask with surrounding tissue. Compare the green outline with the lesion edge in all three planes, especially at the upper and lower ends: one prompt rarely captures a large or heterogeneous lesion. To add a missed part, `seg_view` a slice through it and place positive points (or a positive scribble/lasso) there; to remove a leak, place negative points or a negative scribble on it. `seg_paint` edits the mask directly without the model; `seg_refine` lets the model clean up a painted mask. `seg_edit` does component and morphology edits. `seg_undo`/`seg_checkout` restore earlier versions. `seg_candidates` lists automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong, so judge each by the tissue inside its outline. `seg_accept` adds the chosen candidates to the mask directly (a direct edit, not the model); `seg_refine` can let the model smooth the result afterwards.
4. **Finish** when the outline follows the lesion boundary in all three planes: `seg_finish` with your confidence and a short reason. The first `seg_finish` shows a final review (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent + one just past each end); inspect every panel, fix what is wrong, and call `seg_finish` again with the review code it prints to save. The review also shows candidate corrections in a second image: for each, decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept with `seg_accept`, then finish again for a new review) or normal tissue (reject by not accepting it).

Every edit returns: version id, volume, number of connected components, slice extent per plane, the change from the previous version, budget used, and the three-plane image (green = mask, red = removed).

## Rules
- **What counts as the lesion.** Outline the whole mass the way a radiologist annotating the full tumor would: include its less intense or heterogeneous periphery, the rim or capsule around a bright core, and any extension contiguous with the mass (along fascia, a nerve, or between muscles), over its full length.
- Segment the whole lesion described in the task, and nothing else. If it is multifocal, include all parts.
- Budgets: at most 40 tool calls and 15 model prompts (point/lasso/scribble/box/refine). Every call counts, including views and calls that fail. When the tool-call budget is used up, only `seg_finish` works. Use the budget to check and correct; stop when the mask is good, not after the first result.
- Keep working until you call `seg_finish`. Do not stop to ask questions; nobody will answer.
- Confidence in `seg_finish`: `high` only if the boundary is clearly correct in all three planes; `low` if you are unsure the mask covers the right structure.

toolsAdded.name: seg_accept
toolsAdded.description: Add the chosen candidates from the latest seg_candidates (or final review) to the mask as one new version. A direct edit without the model (seg_refine can smooth it afterwards). Only accept candidates whose tissue is part of the lesion. Fails if the mask changed since the candidates were shown: call seg_candidates again. Counts as a tool call, not a model prompt.

toolsAdded.name: seg_box
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a 2D box. Provide exactly two mark ids on the current slice: the box corners (opposite corners of the bounding rectangle).

ids.description: Exactly two mark ids: the box corners.

toolsAdded.name: seg_candidates
toolsAdded.description: List automatic proposals (C1, C2, ...) of lesion tissue the current mask may have missed, computed from image intensity only; they are often wrong. Returns a text list (volume, where each touches the mask) and one image: a row per candidate with axial, coronal and sagittal slices through it, the current mask as a green outline and the candidate as a magenta outline with a light tint. Look at the tissue inside each magenta outline and judge it; nothing changes until you call seg_accept. Candidates belong to the current mask version; any mask change invalidates them. Counts as a tool call.

toolsAdded.name: seg_checkout
toolsAdded.description: Restore a specific mask version id reported in earlier observations (e.g. v3).

toolsAdded.name: seg_edit
toolsAdded.description: Non-model mask edit. keep_component/remove_component need a mark id inside the component. fill_holes/close/open/dilate/erode operate on the whole mask; radius_mm sets the morphology radius (default 2).

toolsAdded.name: seg_finish
toolsAdded.description: Save the final mask and end the case. The first call (without review_code) shows a final review of the current mask (five slices per plane: three inside the mask extent and one just past each end), a second image with candidate corrections (possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask: accept those that belong with seg_accept, then review again) and a review code. Check it, fix problems, then call seg_finish again with that review_code to save. Editing after the review requires a new review.

review_code.description: Code printed in the latest final review; required to save.

toolsAdded.name: seg_lasso
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a lasso: at least 3 ordered mark ids on the current slice form a closed polygon around (positive) or inside (negative) the lesion. Prefer this over many points for a rough outline.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_open
toolsAdded.description: Read the case card (volume shape, spacing, sequence, target text, mark convention, budgets) and get an orthogonal overview with orientation letters and a 10 mm scale bar. Call this first.

toolsAdded.name: seg_paint
toolsAdded.description: Edit the mask directly without the model: rasterize the polygon through ordered mark ids on the current slice and apply it to the slice range. mode add fills, mode erase removes. Use seg_refine afterwards to let the model clean the painted boundary.

ids.description: At least 3 mark ids on the current slice, listed in order around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); the polygon connects them in this order and closes back to the first.

slice_range.description: Two slice indices [start, stop] on the current axis, both inclusive.

toolsAdded.name: seg_point
toolsAdded.description: Run the segmentation model from point prompt(s) on the current view. Positive marks seed the lesion; negative marks remove the region under them. Adds to the current mask.

ids.description: Mark ids shown in the current seg_view, in order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_refine
toolsAdded.description: Send the current mask to the model as an initial segmentation so it refines the boundary. Use after seg_paint or a rough lasso.

toolsAdded.name: seg_scribble
toolsAdded.description: Run the model from a scribble: ordered mark ids on the current slice form a polyline. Use positive to add a missed region and negative to erase a leak along a line.

ids.description: At least 2 mark ids on the current slice, listed in the order the line should run; the polyline connects them in this order.

toolsAdded.name: seg_sheet
toolsAdded.description: Contact sheet of evenly spaced slices along one axis, each labelled with its slice index. Use it to locate the lesion, then inspect single slices with seg_view.

toolsAdded.name: seg_undo
toolsAdded.description: Restore the parent of the current mask version.

toolsAdded.name: seg_view
toolsAdded.description: Show one slice as a clean panel and a marked panel. Clean + marked are returned side by side. All mark ids refer to the view returned last. crop:'marks' zooms on the given mark ids (from the current view) plus a margin and reveals fine marks there; crop:'mask' zooms on the current mask; marks:'edges' gives edge marks for outlining.

ids.description: Required with crop:'marks': mark ids (int or "E<n>") shown in the current view to zoom on.

content.text:
Case M24: segment the myxoid soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 280x280x330 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.

case M24 | sequence T2 | shape (i,j,k)=(280, 280, 330) | spacing 1x1x1 mm
target: myxoid soft-tissue tumor
display: radiological. axial: patient right LEFT, anterior TOP. coronal: patient right LEFT, superior TOP. sagittal: anterior LEFT, superior TOP. R/L cannot be verified for single limbs.
pointing: set-of-marks only. Global marks are integer IDs (3D); edge marks are 'E<n>' valid only in the current view. Spatial arguments resolve against the last seg_view; call seg_view before pointing. Slice indices are navigation.
lasso/scribble/paint: list mark IDs IN ORDER around the outline (clockwise or counter-clockwise); an out-of-order list self-intersects and fills with holes.
budgets: 40 tool calls, 15 model prompts (exhausted -> call seg_finish).
axial 165/330 | crop full | marks none | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 1/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: This looks like a limb with a small cross-section, so I should check the axial images to locate the lesion.

content.text: sheet axial 60–300/330 (16 slices) | v0 | tool calls 2/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking: I'm tracking the bright T2 hyperintense mass spanning the axial slices, consistent with a myxoid tumor appearance, and cross-checking its shape against the coronal and sagittal views to confirm the lesion's extent.

content.text: sheet coronal 90–190/280 (12 slices) | v0 | tool calls 3/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking:
Looking at the coronal view, there's a distinct bright structure extending superior to inferior through the middle of the image. The axial slices reveal a large homogeneous ovoid mass spanning roughly 172-220, which raises the possibility of a myxoid tumor, plus another bright area at 140-156 on what appears to be the patient's right side given standard display orientation.

That crescent-shaped bright region in the upper-left on axial 140 and 156 might be a separate structure, maybe muscle or fluid — I should pull up axial 180 at full resolution to get a clearer look.

content.text: axial 180/330 | crop full | marks coarse | overlay none | v0 | tool calls 4/40, prompts 0/15

content.thinking:
The image is dark with a small body outline, and the bright round mass looks like the myxoid tumor showing T2 hyperintensity against darker surrounding muscle. I'll seed a point at a central bright location, trying mark 154 or 150.

I notice the lower-right bright region near 150/141 is brightest, while the upper-left near 144/156 is moderately bright, so maybe a point at 143 and 136 would capture it better. I should also check whether that upper-left lobe represents a separate compartment rather than part of the same mass, but for now I'll place a point prompt and see how it segments.

content.text: version v1 (parent v0) | volume 427.5 mL | components 19 (largest 99.9%; 18 others total 0.6 mL) | extent axial 84–270, coronal 84–155, sagittal 106–193 | change +427.5 mL / 0.0 mL | tool calls 5/40, prompts 1/15 | point add (1 mark(s)) | image: axial 175, coronal 121, sagittal 148 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking:
The 427 mL volume seems large, but the mask does capture the bright mass well across sagittal and coronal views, with 19 components where the largest covers 99.9%. Checking the axial extent more closely, the mask spans slices 84–270, but that seems to extend beyond where the bright mass actually ends around slice 236, so I want to verify the boundary isn't overreaching.

I'm also noticing the coronal view shows the mask tapering into an inferior tail at slices 117, 126, and 135, which could reflect infiltrative tumor or edema-like tissue typical of myxoid lesions, so I should confirm whether this tail is genuinely part of the mass. I'll check the mask overlay on axial slices 140 and 156 where the upper-left lobe appeared to make sure nothing's missing.

content.text: axial 140/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 6/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At axial 140, I notice the mask includes the central bright mass plus a separate oval lobe at the upper-left, patient right anterior region, slightly dimmer and divided from the main mass by a dark boundary line — possibly a distinct structure like muscle rather than tumor tissue.

Actually, tracing the mask boundary more carefully, it seems to enclose both the upper-left oval and the main mass, separated by a dark cleft that's excluded from the mask itself. The upper-left oval's intensity resembles the main mass more than surrounding dark muscle tissue, so it might be part of the tumor rather than a separate anatomical structure, though I can't be certain — I should check how this oval appears across other slices like 124, 156, 172, and 204 to get a clearer picture before examining segmentation candidates.

content.text: axial 124/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 7/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
Looking at axial slice 124, the mask covers the main mass plus a thin strip at the upper-left that could be muscle or fascia, along with a small fragment near the lower-left edge of the mass. I'm trying to work out whether that dim strip of tissue should really be included in the mask or if it's separate from the mass.

I'm comparing to the oval structure seen at slice 140 to check if they're connected, and the sagittal/coronal views to confirm the lesion's superior-inferior extent. Overall the mask looks reasonable, but I need to check whether the anterior-right oval is actually part of the tumor, so I'll pull up axial 156 with the outline overlaid to verify.

content.text: axial 156/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 8/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At axial 156, the anatomy looks more complex with multiple compartments: an upper-right mass of intermediate signal, a dark central septum, a bright posterior-lower region, and a bright lateral left region, plus the upper-left oval on patient right. The lobulated, bright appearance with septations makes me wonder if this could be a myxoid tumor with a multi-compartment structure.

Given the dark subcutaneous fat, this is probably a fat-suppressed T2 or STIR sequence, where normal muscle appears dark-grey and myxoid/fluid tissue appears bright—so the bright posterior mass likely represents the tumor itself, while the grey anterior oval could be adjacent muscle, suggesting this might be imaging of a thigh or lower leg.

I'm trying to map out which regions are tumor versus normal muscle: the bright crescent laterally, the intermediate-intensity anterior region with a darker center (possibly fibrous septa within heterogeneous myxoid tumor), and the upper-left grey oval that looks homogeneous with a rim, likely muscle rather than tumor based on its intensity matching surrounding tissue.

Checking slices further inferiorly (180, 204, 220), the mass appears uniformly bright and round, suggesting those slices capture the tumor cleanly, while the more complex, lobed appearance at 140-156 may reflect a muscle compartment being displaced or compressed by the tumor rather than tumor itself. Given limited tool calls remaining, I want to view axial slice 148 with an outline overlay to better see the transition between the muscle-like oval and the tumor mass.

content.text: axial 172/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 9/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At slice 172, the entire round structure appears as a single homogeneous mass with a bright posterior region and grey anterior, and the mask boundary covering it looks reasonable when checked against the coordinates.

The upper-left oval seen at 156 likely merges with this round mass at 172 as part of the same lesion envelope, so I want to verify the inferior extent around 204-270 and the superior extent around 84-110, along with checking coronal slices 84-155 and the sagittal view to confirm the mask boundaries hold up across all planes.

content.text: axial 236/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 10/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: At slice 236 the mask looks fine around the round mass, aside from a couple small stray components near (925,445) and (955,480) that should get cleaned up later by keeping only the largest component. I'm now checking the lower slices around 252-260 where the structure tapers into a vessel-like tail, estimating the mass likely ends around slice 240-245.

content.text: axial 252/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 11/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: At slice 252, the mask is just a small stray blob rather than the actual tumor since the bright structure there is vessels or fascia. I should remove these small components and keep only the main one, so I'll use keep_component marking inside the largest region, like at mark 154, as a non-model edit.

content.thinking: I need a mark in the current view, but the current axial 252 crop mask has no marks. Let me check an axial slice inside the mass, like 180, with coarse segmentation overlay to add one.

content.text: axial 190/330 | crop mask | marks coarse | overlay outline | v1 | tool calls 13/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking: The axial 190 mask looks like it covers the round mass well, so I'll keep the component at mark 155 since it's inside the mass, then still need to check the tail region around axial 240-270.

content.text: version v2 (parent v1) | volume 426.9 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 84–247, coronal 84–155, sagittal 106–193 | change +0.0 mL / -0.6 mL | tool calls 14/40, prompts 1/15 | edit keep_component | image: axial 175, coronal 121, sagittal 148 through mask centre (green = new mask, red = removed)

content.thinking: I'm checking whether the mask's superior extent at axial 84-110 actually belongs to the tumor, comparing the bright center region seen at slice 108 and the ring-like structures at slice 92 to confirm the upper boundary.

content.text: axial 108/330 | crop mask | marks none | overlay outline | v2 | tool calls 15/40, prompts 1/15

content.thinking:
At axial 108 the mask covers a dim grey region that could be the tumor's superior tip rather than muscle, so the top of the lesion is probably closer to slices 110-115 with partial volume effects making this boundary a bit uncertain.

I'm also looking at an upper-left oval seen across axial 140-172 — it merges with the main mass at lower slices but appears separated by a dark line around 156. Given the "whole mass" rule and its contiguity lower down, it seems reasonable to include it as a lobule of the myxoid tumor rather than muscle. I'll spend one call checking seg_candidates for any missed tissue.

C1 add 237 mL, touches mask on its anterior, left and posterior sides, mostly inferior of the mask

content.thinking:
I'm looking at C1, the peripheral rim around the mass — grey intermediate tissue at axial 156 that looks like surrounding muscle or fascia, possibly edema, but it's large at 237 mL which makes me question whether it fits the criteria for a normal periphery.

Checking the other candidate pieces: C2 posterior thin band, C3 superior thin band, C4 and C5 small fragments — all look like muscle or fascia, so I'm rejecting them too, leaving no accepts among these peripheral pieces.

The mask boundary generally seems to track the bright mass edges well, and the anterior-right oval region is already included appropriately, so I think it's time to do one more confirmation at a mid-slice like axial 200 before calling the segmentation finish review.

arguments.reason: Single large T2-bright lobulated mass segmented from one intensity-based point prompt, cleaned to one component; boundary matches bright mass in axial, coronal and sagittal views. Uncertainty: upper-anterior oval lobe near axial 140-156 and superior tip near axial 108 are of intermediate intensity and included; peripheral candidate rims judged as muscle and rejected.

content.text:
Final review of v2: volume 426.9 mL | components 1 (largest 100.0%) | extent axial 84–247, coronal 84–155, sagittal 106–193 | tool calls 17/40, prompts 1/15. The image shows five slices per plane (three inside the mask extent + one just past each end; past-the-mask panels are orange). Check: (1) Is lesion tissue visible in the past-the-mask panels (orange)? Then the mask stops too early: seg_view that slice and add positive points on the lesion there. (2) Does the outline cut through lesion or include normal tissue on any panel? (3) Stray components? If any answer shows a problem, fix it before finishing. Candidates (second image): automatic proposals of possibly missed lesion tissue next to the mask, computed from image intensity only (often wrong).

For each candidate decide whether the tissue inside its outline is part of the same lesion (accept) or normal tissue (reject). Accept with seg_accept and call seg_finish again for a new review; if none belong, confirm with the review code. If everything is right, call seg_finish again with review_code "4971" to save it.

content.thinking:
Checking the final panels confirms no lesion tissue past the mask boundaries, so that's settled. For candidate C1, the rim around the mass in axial 156 looks like a thick magenta band blending into grey muscle tissue rather than a distinct lesion margin, so I'm rejecting it. Now I want to double-check axial 125 before finalizing.

Looking across axial 172 and 156, the mask boundary seems tight against the bright mass region with surrounding muscle appearing dark, and C1's periphery band is roughly 5-10mm thick — comparing this to the tighter boundary at 172, I'll reject C1 and finish with review code 4971.

arguments.reason: One connected lesion mask following the bright T2 mass in all planes; past-the-mask panels contain no lesion tissue. Candidate rims C1-C5 look like surrounding muscle/fascia and were rejected. Moderate confidence because the anterior oval lobe and superior tip are intermediate intensity.

content.text: case M24 finished (confidence medium); final mask saved from v2 | final volume 426.9 mL, components 1 (largest 100.0%) | tool calls 18/40, prompts 1/15
Case finished. The final mask has been saved; do not call any more tools.

I segmented the myxoid tumour as one connected mask of about 427 mL and saved it with medium confidence.

- **Mask:** a single positive point on the bright T2 mass produced the initial result. I removed 19 small stray pieces, including one near the lower end that was vessel or fascia, so only the main mass remains. The mask spans axial slices 84–247, coronal 84–155 and sagittal 106–193.
- **Checks:** the outline follows the bright mass edge in the axial, coronal and sagittal views I inspected. The final review showed no lesion tissue beyond either end of the mask.
- **Rejected candidates:** the five automatic candidates (C1–C5) were thin rims or small pieces that look like surrounding muscle or fascia, so I did not add them. The largest one (C1, about 237 mL) is a ring of intermediate-grey tissue around the mass.
- **Uncertainty:** the anterior-right oval lobe (around axial 140–156) and the superior tip (around axial 108) have intermediate intensity. I included both because they connect to the main mass at lower levels. If either is normal tissue, the mask is slightly too large there.

Tool use was 18 of 40 calls and 1 of 15 model prompts.
